sources.citation: Pentair/SHURflo doc 911-415 REV.K 4/09 (ECO# 16282), '9300 Series Submersible Pump D.C. Powered — Owners Manual'. Technical Specifications p.16 names MODEL NUMBER 9325-043-101 explicitly. — https://s1.solacity.com/docs/S

transport: Two conductors. #10 AWG jacketed submersible cable, flat-parallel or round, terminated into a screw-set plug/receptacle cable adapter at the pump. 911-415 Rev.K p.3 step 2b instructs the installer to 'Cut ONE of the lead wires 1.0 in.' to stagger the pair — there are exactly two. 24 VDC nominal, 120 W, 4.0 A max, 7.5 A automotive fuse.
refutedOnReview: REFUTED. The cited source exists and is authentic, and it does name the model — but it documents no register map of any kind, because the device has no digital interface. Source is genuine. 19 pages
gotchas: Filed separately from the diaphragm pumps because the control semantics differ, not because of the model number: the 9300 has no pressure switch at all. It has a mechanical internal bypass at 105-110 PSI and it runs whenever the LCB feeds it power. Everything about when it starts and stops lives in the controller, so a

911-415 Rev.K p.2 lists the controller under 'Components needed for installation': 'CONTROLLER: Use of an LCB (Linear Current Booster) Unit is required for optimum performance.' The 902-100 and 902-200 are those units. This is the vendor naming the pairing, which is why the two dialects are recorded together.

This pump is the one on the retailer list that is actually an off-grid solar product rather than an RV/marine one — 24 V, 230 ft (70 m) max lift, 100 ft (30 m) max submersion, and the whole manual is drawn around a solar array feeding a controller feeding a well.

A WebFetch summariser asserted during this sweep that the 9300 uses 'a 4-conductor submersible cable' for 'power delivery and system communication'. Reading the actual PDF shows a two-conductor cable and no communication of any kind. Recorded because it is exactly the fabricated-fact failure mode the catalogue rules ex
unmappedReports: Pump run state — same `pump-run-state` gap as the diaphragm dialect., Well drawdown / static water level. The vendor's own application worksheet is built on H1 discharge head, H2 water level, H3 submergence and 'draw down'. `tank-level` and `tank-volume` exist for tanks; nothing models a well's water column, which is the number that actually predicts whether this pump is about to run dry.
